title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes and recent hypoglycemia.

HPI
The patient is a 62-year-old individual presenting for a routine follow-up regarding their diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient reports that they have been managed on long-term insulin therapy. They report a recent hypoglycemic episode that occurred approximately three days ago. The patient states they felt shaky and lightheaded but recovered after consuming a snack. They currently do not take any other medications for their glucose management.

Medication List
- Insulin (long-term)

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Skin is warm and dry. Neurological exam shows intact sensation and motor function in all extremities. Vital signs are stable.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
2. Hypoglycemia.

Plan
The patient will continue their current insulin regimen. We discussed the importance of monitoring blood glucose levels more frequently to prevent future occurrences of hypoglycemia. The patient was instructed to carry a fast-acting carbohydrate source at all times. Follow-up in four weeks.
explanations: Diabetes with hypoglycemia and no coma documented: E11.649.
Long-term insulin use in type 2 diabetes: add Z79.4.

distractors.why: Hypoglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Z79.4 is required for routine insulin use in type 2 diabetes.
